column1: request|To ask for something formally or politely.|I would like to request a copy of the agreement.
apologise|To say that you are sorry about something.|I apologise for missing our scheduled meeting.
complain|To express dissatisfaction about a problem.|I am writing to complain about the delayed repair.
explain|To make a situation or idea easier to understand.|Please explain why the booking was cancelled.
confirm|To state that an arrangement or detail is correct.|Please confirm the date of my appointment.
inform|To give someone information.|I am writing to inform you of my new address.
notify|To formally tell someone about something.|Please notify the office if your contact details change.
advise|To give guidance or useful information.|Could you advise me on the available evening classes?
suggest|To put forward an idea for consideration.|I suggest moving the meeting to the community hall.
recommend|To say that a particular option would be suitable.|I would recommend the morning session for beginners.
invite|To ask someone to attend or take part.|We would like to invite you to the neighbourhood meeting.
accept|To agree to an invitation or offer.|I am pleased to accept your offer of a place.
decline|To politely refuse an invitation or offer.|Unfortunately, I must decline the invitation because of work.
arrange|To make plans for something to happen.|Could we arrange a convenient time for the inspection?
postpone|To move a planned activity to a later time.|We need to postpone the appointment until next week.
cancel|To stop a planned arrangement from taking place.|Please cancel my booking for Friday evening.
attend|To be present at an event or meeting.|I will be able to attend the induction on Monday.
participate|To take part in an activity.|I would like to participate in the volunteer programme.
provide|To give something needed or requested.|Please provide details of the course timetable.
supply|To make goods or information available.|Could you supply a replacement instruction booklet?
attach|To include a document with a message.|Please attach your receipt to the email.
enclose|To place a document inside a letter or package.|I enclose a copy of the signed application form.
forward|To send a message or document on to someone else.|Please forward this message to the property manager.
reply|To respond to a message or question.|Could you reply before the registration deadline?
respond|To give an answer or reaction.|Please respond using the contact details below.
follow up|To make further contact about an earlier matter.|I am writing to follow up on my repair request.
contact|To communicate with someone.|Please contact me if you need any further information.
reach|To successfully contact someone.|You can reach me by phone after five.
address a concern|To deal with an issue someone has raised.|The manager promised to address a concern about noise.
resolve|To find a satisfactory solution to a problem.|I hope we can resolve this matter promptly.
replace|To provide something in place of another item.|Could you replace the damaged shelf?
refund request|A formal request for money to be returned.|I have attached the receipt to my refund request.
inconvenience|Trouble or difficulty caused by a situation.|I apologise for any inconvenience caused by the change.
disappointment|Unhappiness because something was not as expected.|I would like to express my disappointment with the service.
concern|A matter that causes worry or needs attention.|My main concern is the lack of safe access.
assistance|Help with a task or problem.|I would appreciate your assistance with this application.
understanding|Willingness to recognise another person's situation.|Thank you for your understanding during this difficult week.
cooperative|Willing to work with others to solve a problem.|Your staff were cooperative when I reported the fault.
polite|Showing consideration and respect for others.|A polite request is more suitable than a demand.
formal|Suitable for official or professional communication.|Use a formal greeting when writing to the council.
informal|Suitable for relaxed communication with someone familiar.|An informal message is appropriate when inviting a close friend.
appropriate|Suitable for a particular situation.|Please suggest an appropriate time for the meeting.
relevant|Connected to the matter being discussed.|Include any relevant booking information in your reply.
specific|Clear and exact rather than general.|Give a specific date when describing the delivery problem.
clear|Easy to understand.|Please give clear instructions for collecting the keys.
accurate|Correct and free from mistakes.|Make sure the account details are accurate.
detailed|Including plenty of specific information.|A detailed description will help the technician prepare.
brief|Short in length or duration.|Please send a brief explanation of the change.
additional|Extra to what has already been provided.|Let me know if you need additional documents.
further|More or extra.|I would welcome further information about the placement.
regarding|Concerning a particular subject.|I am writing regarding my recent equipment hire.
concerning|About a particular matter.|Please contact me concerning the proposed timetable.
in response to|As a reply to something.|I am writing in response to your vacancy advertisement.
in advance|Before something happens or is needed.|Please let us know in advance if you cannot attend.
as soon as possible|At the earliest practical time.|Please arrange the repair as soon as possible.
look forward to|To anticipate something with pleasure.|I look forward to hearing from you.
would appreciate|A polite way to say that something would be welcome.|I would appreciate a written confirmation of the booking.
be grateful|To feel thankful for help or consideration.|I would be grateful if you could check the invoice.
unfortunately|Used to introduce disappointing information.|Unfortunately, I cannot attend the session on Tuesday.
fortunately|Used to introduce a helpful or positive circumstance.|Fortunately, I can attend the alternative session on Friday.
however|Used to introduce a contrasting point.|The room was clean; however, the heating did not work.
therefore|For that reason.|The item is faulty; therefore, I am requesting a replacement.
although|Used to introduce a contrasting fact.|Although I booked early, the requested room was unavailable.
despite|Even though a particular difficulty or fact exists.|Despite several calls, I have not received an update.
because of|As a result of something.|I need to reschedule because of a change to my rota.
due to|Caused by or resulting from.|The event was postponed due to heavy rain.
in addition|Used to add another point.|In addition, the parcel arrived without instructions.
otherwise|If the suggested action is not taken.|Please reply by Friday; otherwise, we may lose the booking.
meanwhile|During the time before something else happens.|Meanwhile, could you provide a temporary heater?
initially|At the beginning.|Initially, I was told that delivery would take two days.
finally|After earlier events or at the last stage.|The replacement finally arrived yesterday.
regret|To feel sorry about a situation or decision.|I regret that I must cancel my attendance.
guaranteed response|A reply promised within a specified period.|The service advertises a guaranteed response within two working days.
reasonable|Fair and sensible in the circumstances.|I believe a replacement would be a reasonable solution.
availability|The times or circumstances in which something is obtainable.|Please let me know your availability next week.
alternative|Another possible choice.|Could you offer an alternative appointment?
arrangement|A plan agreed between people.|Please confirm our arrangement to collect the keys on Monday.
attachment|A file included with an electronic message.|The attachment contains a photograph of the damage.
recipient|The person intended to receive a message or item.|Please check the recipient before sending confidential information.
signature|A person's written name confirming identity or agreement.|Please add your signature to the application form.
clarify|To make unclear information easier to understand.|Could you clarify whether the fee includes materials?
propose|To formally suggest a plan or action.|We propose extending the library's opening hours.
acknowledge|To confirm that something has been received or noticed.|Kindly acknowledge receipt of this application.
rectify|To put right an error or problem.|Please rectify the incorrect charge on my statement.
appreciation|Recognition of help or something done well.|I would like to express my appreciation for your support.
gratitude|A feeling of thankfulness.|Please accept my gratitude for arranging the extra session.
consideration|Careful attention given to a request or issue.|Thank you for your consideration of my request.
courteous|Respectful and considerate in behaviour.|The receptionist was courteous despite the busy queue.
semi-formal|Polite but less distant than fully formal communication.|Use a semi-formal tone when writing to a familiar supervisor.
concise|Expressed clearly using few words.|Keep the opening explanation concise.
with reference to|Referring to a particular previous matter.|With reference to our call, I confirm the revised date.
at your convenience|At a time that suits you.|Please call me at your convenience to discuss the options.
subsequently|After the event just mentioned.|I paid the fee and subsequently received confirmation.
promptly|Without unnecessary delay.|I would appreciate it if you could respond promptly.
assure|To tell someone confidently that something is true.|I assure you that the equipment was used correctly.
satisfactory|Good enough to meet the relevant need or expectation.|The repair has not produced a satisfactory result.
unsatisfactory|Not good enough for the expected purpose.|I am writing about the unsatisfactory condition of the room.
commitment|An obligation or promise that needs to be fulfilled.|A work commitment prevents me from attending.
circumstance|A fact or condition affecting a situation.|Please explain any circumstance that affects your application.
salutation|The greeting at the beginning of a letter.|Choose a salutation that matches your relationship with the reader.
